title: Setu Expense Tracker vs Zoho Expense: Which One Does Your Business Actually Need?
seoTitle: Setu Expense Tracker vs Zoho Expense (2026)
metaDescription: Zoho Expense processes staff claims and prices by seat with a five-user minimum; Setu's Expense Tracker is a free browser log. An honest 2026 comparison.
excerpt: Zoho Expense is a claims-and-reimbursement platform priced per seat, with a three-user free tier and a five-seat minimum on paid plans. Setu's Expense Tracker is a free browser log for the owner who pays the bills. Here is which trade fits your business.
keywords: setu expense tracker vs zoho expense
free expense tracker for small business India

faq.question: Is Setu's Expense Tracker free, and is there a catch?
faq.answer: It is free with no account and no limit on entries. The trade is that everything stays in your browser, so it is a single-user record and you should export the CSV periodically rather than treating the browser as permanent storage.

faq.question: How many users does Zoho Expense's free plan allow?
faq.answer: Three, as publicly listed in September 2026, along with 20 receipt autoscans per user each month and 5 GB of receipt storage. Paid tiers start at a five-user minimum, so a fourth user effectively means buying five seats.

faq.question: Can I use both together?
faq.answer: Yes, and some businesses do. Staff claims run through the platform while the owner keeps a separate quick log of direct shop spending. Just make sure only one of the two feeds your accounts, or the same rupee gets counted twice.

faq.question: Does the Expense Tracker do receipt scanning?
faq.answer: No. You type the amount, date, category and a short note. For a handful of entries a day that is faster than photographing and correcting an OCR result; for dozens of travel bills a week it is not, and that is the point where a scanning platform earns its fee.

faq.question: What happens to my data if I clear my browser?
faq.answer: It goes. Export to CSV at the end of each month and keep the file with your other records. That habit also gives your accountant something to work from without asking you to reconstruct the month from memory.

bodyHtml:
Two products, one word in the name, and almost nothing else in common. Zoho Expense is an employee expense-and-reimbursement platform: staff submit claims, managers approve them, finance reimburses. Setu's Expense Tracker is a free browser log for the person who actually pays the bills — one owner, one list, no approvals.

Most comparison posts pretend these are the same product at different prices. They are not. Picking well is mostly about being honest with yourself about who in your business spends money, and whether anyone needs to say yes before they do.

What Zoho Expense is built to do

Zoho Expense automates the claim cycle. An employee photographs a bill, the OCR reads the amount, date and merchant, the expense lands in a report, a policy rule flags it if it breaks a limit, an approver signs off, and the reimbursement is pushed out and posted to your accounting system. On the higher tier it also handles travel booking, per diem rates and live mileage capture.

That chain is worth real money when you have field staff, a sales team, or anyone spending company money away from the counter. It replaces a WhatsApp group full of photographed bills and a spreadsheet somebody maintains on Sundays. If that is your problem, a dedicated expense platform is the right shape of tool and this post is not going to talk you out of it.

What it costs, as publicly listed in September 2026

Zoho lists three tiers on its India pricing page. The figures below are what was published in September 2026 — check zoho.com/in/expense/pricing before you budget, because tiers and limits move.

PlanListed priceUsersReceipt autoscans
Free₹0Up to 320 per user per month
Standard₹79 per user/month billed annually, ₹99 monthlyMinimum 5200 per user per month
Premium₹149 per user/month billed annually, ₹199 monthlyMinimum 51,000 per user per month

Two details in that table decide more than the headline rate. The first is the three-user ceiling on the free plan: it is a genuine free tier, not a trial, but a fourth person ends the arrangement. The second is the five-user minimum on the paid tiers. A business with two people who need it still pays for five, so the realistic entry cost is about ₹395 a month on annual billing rather than the ₹79 the price list leads with. That is not a criticism — it is how seat-based software is sold — but it is the number that belongs in your budget.

What Setu's Expense Tracker does instead

The Expense Tracker answers a narrower question: where did the money go this month? You add an expense with a date, a category, an amount and a note. It totals by category, totals by month, and exports to CSV. There is no login, no seat count and no approval step, because the data lives in your browser rather than on a server anyone has to pay for.

That design has an obvious ceiling and one underrated strength. The ceiling: it is a single-user record. Nobody submits anything to you, nothing gets approved, and the data does not follow you to another device unless you export it. The strength: it takes about nine seconds per entry and costs nothing, which means it actually gets used. A perfect claims workflow nobody fills in is worth less than a rough list that is current.

Alongside it, the Cash Book handles daily cash in and out with running balances, and the Profit Dashboard puts those expenses next to your sales and product costs so the month ends with a profit figure rather than a pile of receipts. If you are trying to hold spending to a plan, Budget vs Actual shows the variance by category as you type.

Side by side

DimensionSetu Expense TrackerZoho Expense

UsersOne, on one browser3 free, then 5-seat minimum
ApprovalsNonePolicy rules and approval chains
Receipt scanningNo — you type the amountYes, with monthly scan limits
ReimbursementOutside the toolBuilt in on paid tiers
Data locationYour browserZoho's servers, multi-device
CostFree, no signupFree to 3 users, then per seat

Three shops, three answers

A single-outlet shop or restaurant where the owner pays for everything. Nobody claims anything, so the approval machinery is overhead with a monthly fee attached. The free tracker plus a disciplined weekly habit is genuinely enough, and the CSV goes to your accountant at month end.

A two-to-three person office with occasional travel. This is the awkward middle. Zoho's free tier covers you at exactly three users, which works until you hire. If the spending is occasional, a shared expense log and a WhatsApp folder of bills still beats paying for five seats. If someone is on the road every week, the scanning alone earns its keep.

Field staff, sales reps or multiple outlet managers spending company money. Buy the platform. The thing you are actually paying for is the control — a limit that gets enforced before the money leaves, an approver on record, and an audit trail you did not have to assemble. A browser log cannot give you any of that, and pretending otherwise costs more than the subscription.

The question behind the question

Before you compare features, work out which of these two sentences describes your month. Money leaves the business and I want to know where it went. That is a record-keeping problem, and a list solves it. Money leaves the business through other people and I want a say before it does. That is a control problem, and only software with approvals solves it. Buying a control tool for a record-keeping problem is the most common way small businesses overspend on software.

There is a third sentence worth naming, because it hides behind the other two: money left the business and it never reached the books. No expense tool fixes that on its own. Whether the entry sits in a browser log or a seat-based platform, someone still has to post it to the right account, match it against the bank, and close the month. If that step is not happening, adding a subscription changes the storage location of the problem and nothing else.

A rough test: count the people who spend company money without asking you first. Zero means the free tracker is the whole answer. One or two, occasionally, and Zoho's three-user free tier probably covers you until you hire. Three or more, regularly, and you are past what any single-user log can carry — not because the log is bad, but because the thing you need is a second signature, and a list cannot give you one.

The migration nobody mentions

Because the Setu tool keeps data in your browser, moving off it is an export, not a negotiation: CSV out, CSV in, done. Moving off a seat-based platform after two years is a bigger job, and it is worth asking early what the export looks like — whether attachments come with the data or only the line items. That question costs nothing to ask during a sales call and a great deal to ask afterwards.

The same logic applies in reverse. If you start free and grow into a platform, having a year of clean, categorised expense history in CSV makes the setup faster, because your category list already reflects how you actually spend rather than a default template.

The honest verdict

If the question is who spent this and did anyone approve it, you need Zoho Expense or something like it, and the five-seat minimum is the price of that answer. If the question is what did we spend this month and on what, the free tracker answers it completely and the subscription buys you machinery you will not switch on.

The failure mode we see most is a two-person business paying for five seats of a claims platform to solve a bookkeeping problem — and still not knowing its monthly profit, because nothing was ever posted to a proper set of books. If that sounds familiar, the tool is not the gap. Our accounting and bookkeeping service exists for exactly that case: someone else closes the month while you run the shop.
